description: The JOIN forms and the LATERAL keyword over a three-employee, three-department fixture. CROSS JOIN and the comma spelling both produce the cartesian product; INNER JOIN matches on the key; LEFT and LEFT OUTER keep every left row null-extended; RIGHT keeps the unmatched departments; FULL OUTER keeps both sides' orphans. A LATERAL subquery is evaluated per left row, so it correlates - and with an extra filter inside it, it drops the rows that no longer match. Multi-table joins, table aliases, a subquery in FROM, a join to a subquery, a WHERE beside a join, and multi-condition ON clauses all read. Converted 1:1 from query/JoinAndLateralTest (now retired); the Java asserted a row COUNT for fifteen of its eighteen tests and read cells for only three, so the converted tests name the rows - a LEFT JOIN keeping the right NUMBER of rows but null-extending the wrong one would have passed before.
